newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DIW - 1997 Q1 GDP at 1.5 pct, Q2 at 2.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: German DIW - 1997 Q1 GDP at 1.5 pct, Q2 at 2.5 pct.

text.p: The German economy will show 1.5 percent growth year-on-year in the first quarter of 1997, with growth rising to 2.5 percent in the second quarter, the German Institute for Economic Research (DIW) said on Wednesday.
It added that in east Germany, gross domestic product in the first quarter of 1997 was 4.3 percent up on the previous year, while growth in west Germany was 1.3 percent higher.
In its latest weekly report, the DIW said a slight pickup in growth in the first quarter was due to good weather conditions.
It said the number of people in work had fallen to 43.1 million, while gross income for the employed had stagnated.
It said that for the second quarter, the hope was that an expected rise in new orders from abroad would prompt economic growth through exports in the coming months.
However, in the light of falling domestic demand, the institute warned the economy may also shrink.

But it added that if exports turn out to be as strong as foreign new orders data were currently signalling, gross domestic product could reach 2.5 percent in the second quarter in comparison with a year ago.
